answer: Mirror-Drift Reputation Decay. Each identity's reputation decays toward the median unless refreshed by verified interaction, so mass-created identities stay clustered as a nebula of low-trust nodes. To lift a cluster's aggregate score, an attacker must sustain genuine activity across every identity, paying continuous compute and counterparty fees per identity. Isolated clusters never reach the basalt threshold for high-value actions, so costs scale linearly with fake identity count while returns stay flat.
